title: Midday Brief — Wed 25 Nov

stories.board: New US tariffs hit 14 places, not Canada
stories.headline: US announces new tariffs, and Canada is left out
stories.what: The US proposed new tariffs (extra taxes on goods from other countries) of up to 20 percent on China, the EU, Japan, South Korea and 10 more places. Canada and Mexico are not on the list.
stories.why: Canada dodged this round, and the US trade boss says a deal with Canada is close.
stories.sides: The White House says other countries make too much cheap stuff; critics and right-leaning Townhall warn tariffs could push prices higher.

stories.board: Prices rise faster; tech stocks tumble
stories.headline: Hot inflation report and tariffs knock US stocks down
stories.what: A key US price report showed core inflation (price rises, not counting food and fuel) at 3.3 percent, a bit higher than expected. By midday the Nasdaq was down about 3 percent and Nvidia about 8 percent.
stories.why: Traders now expect the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in December, which makes borrowing cost more.
stories.sides: No major disagreement on the numbers; Townhall points out the economy also grew fast, at 4.3 percent last summer.

stories.board: Judge doubts main Netanyahu corruption charge
stories.headline: Israeli judge says the biggest Netanyahu charge looks weak
stories.what: A judge in Netanyahu's corruption trial said a guilty verdict in the most serious case looks unlikely, and urged a deal (an agreement to end it) in another case. No charges have been dropped yet.
stories.why: It could change Netanyahu's future just as Israel tries to form a new government.
stories.sides: Netanyahu says the trial collapsed; the Attorney General says prosecutors will review it and the case must end in a verdict or a deal.

quick_hits: The US economy grew 4.3 percent in the summer quarter, the fastest in three years.
In Israel, Yair Golan's party paused coalition talks with Eisenkot, who has about 12 days left to form a government.
big_picture: Trade, prices and stocks are shaking things up before American Thanksgiving, but Canada got a break on tariffs.
